summary: Similarity means one shape is an enlargement of another: corresponding angles stay equal and corresponding sides share a single constant ratio (the scale factor). The central obstacle is additive reasoning — treating 'add the same amount to each side' as an enlargement. A 3×5 rectangle grown to 8×10 by adding 5 looks bigger but is not similar, because 8÷3≈2.67 while 10÷5=2. Learners need to see the structure as multiplicative: enlargement from a centre multiplies every vertex's distance from the centre by the scale factor while leaving angles fixed, and a genuinely similar rectangle (e.g. 6×10, each side ×2) must be contrasted with the additive fake.
misconceptions: Additive reasoning: treats 'add the same amount to each side' as an enlargement (3×5 → 8×10 by +5), when similarity requires multiplying each side by a constant
Believes angles get bigger when a shape is enlarged (scales the angles along with the sides)
Uses a different multiplier for different sides, or checks the scale factor on only one pair of corresponding sides and assumes the rest match
Enlarges the shape but does not scale each vertex's distance from the centre of enlargement, so the image is the wrong size or position

activities.title: Grow it by adding, then test whether it stays the same shape
steps: Start with a 3 cm by 5 cm rectangle and predict, in writing, whether making it '8 by 10 by adding 5 to each side' keeps it the same shape just bigger — say yes or no and WHY before checking
Divide each pair of corresponding sides and build a ratio table: 8÷3 ≈ 2.67 beside 10÷5 = 2

Place the 3×5 rectangle on the 8×10 rectangle at a shared corner, with the 3 cm side along the 8 cm side and the 5 cm side along the 10 cm side. Extend the diagonal of the 3×5 that starts at the shared corner and observe whether it passes through the opposite corner of the 8×10 rectangle (it misses it)

Now compare the 3×5 against a 6×10 rectangle: check both ratios (6÷3=2 and 10÷5=2). Then, with the 3 cm side along the 6 cm side at a shared corner, extend the diagonal from that shared corner to see it pass through the opposite corner of the 6×10
State which rectangle is similar to the original and justify using a single shared scale factor
activities.insight: Adding a constant to each side does not in general preserve shape (the only exception is when the sides being compared are equal, as in a square); similarity requires every pair of corresponding sides to reduce to the SAME multiplier. The 8×10 fails the ratio test; the 6×10 (×2) passes.

activities.title: Enlarge from a centre with ray lines
steps: Mark a centre of enlargement and draw rays from it through each vertex of the 3×5 rectangle
Choose a scale factor and multiply EACH vertex's distance from the centre by that factor to place the image vertices
Measure or mark the corresponding angles before and after enlarging, confirming they are unchanged
Fill a ratio table for every pair of corresponding sides, confirming they all reduce to the same scale factor
activities.insight: Enlargement scales distances from a centre by a constant multiplier and preserves angles; the one shared ratio IS the scale factor, which is why the image is similar to the original.

activities.title: Decide similar or not, and find the scale factor
steps: Judge whether 3×5 is similar to 8×10 or to 6×10, giving a reason — and reject 'yes, you added 5 to each side' as a justification
Find a scale factor by dividing a new side length by its corresponding original side
Match corresponding sides between two similar shapes and sort several shape-pairs into 'similar' and 'not similar'
For a stated enlargement by scale factor 3 applied to a triangle, say what happens to its angles (unchanged) and its sides (×3)
activities.insight: The multiplicative test — all corresponding-side ratios equal, angles unchanged — can be applied consistently to classify and quantify similarity.

activities.title: Summary reference: angles equal, sides in one ratio
steps: Reveal, on two overlaid shapes, the corresponding angles marked equal and the corresponding sides labelled with their shared scale factor
Reveal that angles are unchanged under enlargement while each side is multiplied by the scale factor
Re-read a labelled ray-line diagram showing distances from the centre multiplied by the scale factor
activities.insight: Similarity consolidated as a single statement: corresponding angles equal, corresponding sides in one constant ratio, produced by enlargement from a centre.

checkQuestion: Here is a rectangle that is 3 cm by 5 cm. I make a new rectangle that is 8 cm by 10 cm. Is the new rectangle a similar shape to the first one — the same shape, just a different size? Tell me yes or no, and then tell me how you decided.
checkAnswer: No, it is not similar. The corresponding sides are not in the same ratio: 8÷3 ≈ 2.67 but 10÷5 = 2, so there is no single scale factor. (A similar rectangle would be, e.g., 6 by 10 — each side multiplied by 2. The 8×10 was made by ADDING 5 to each side, which does not preserve the shape.)
